extracted.intended_audience: FHFA staff, federal regulators, bank policymakers, and ABA members
extracted.subtask_description: An industry association's formal comment in response to the FHFA's proposed Enterprise Regulatory Capital Framework, offering policy recommendations and concerns about the prescribed leverage buffer (PLBA), credit risk transfer (CRT), and related prudential tools. The letter evaluates potential impacts and requests further analysis and metrics development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce risks held by the Enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: Reducing the risks held by the Enterprises — both during the ongoing conservatorship and in a post-conservatorship environment, is one of the most important responsibilities of the FHFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is framed as a primary objective against which refinements to PLBA, CRT, and other tools should be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-sensitive deployment of prudential tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The tools available and how they can best be deployed will differ under changing circumstances, not least of which include what ultimate form the Enterprises take in a post conservatorship environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHFA should account for differing circumstances (ongoing conservatorship vs post-conservatorship) when designing/refining PLBA and CRT; one-size-fits-all approaches may be inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess impact on management of the Enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed refinements may have significant impacts on the management of the Enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be evaluated for how they will change Enterprise management incentives, risk-taking, and operational decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess impact on availability of mortgage credit to the primary market
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed refinements may have significant impacts on the continued availability of mortgage credit to the primary market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHFA should consider whether refinements would restrict or support access to mortgage credit for primary-market borrowers; effects on liquidity and market functioning should be analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess impact on protection of taxpayers
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed refinements may have significant impacts on the protection of taxpayers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory changes should be judged by their effect on taxpayer exposure and the tradeoffs between private markets and public backstops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess interplay between Enterprises and private mortgage market
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed refinements may have significant impacts on the interplay between the Enterprises and the private mortgage market, both now and in a post-conservatorship environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHFA should evaluate how changes to PLBA and CRT will affect private-label securitization, private capital participation, and the overall private mortgage market structure over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLBA and CRT are important prudential tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Both PLBA and CRT play important roles in the prudential regulation of the Enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any refinement to these tools should recognize their central role and proceed carefully to avoid unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for further refinement supported by additional research
rubrics_metrics.description: The current proposal’s effort to revise and refine the PLBA, CRT and other tools reflected in the current proposal are important steps, but need further refinement, supported by additional research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHFA should commission or rely on additional empirical research before finalizing major changes to ensure proposals are evidence-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop metrics to determine optimal CRT deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of metrics to better determine the degree to which tools such as CRT should be deployed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ABA requests that FHFA develop clear, quantitative metrics to guide when and how much CRT is appropriate, rather than relying solely on qualitative judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions about post-conservatorship corporate structure
rubrics_metrics.description: ABA remains neutral on the question of the appropriate post conservatorship corporate structure of the Enterprises. For purposes of these comments, we presume there will not be legislation enacted in the near term altering the shareholder ownership status that existed prior to conservatorship, and that is the structure to which they will eventually return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses and recommendations in the comment are premised on the assumption of no near-term legislative change to shareholder ownership; FHFA should note this assumption when interpreting the ABA's recommendations.
